headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection and cascading-error via shared filesystem/git: Claude Code can write/execute broadly, while Superset can consume API-driven analytics outputs without documented verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use MCP; its shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress, so if Claude Code writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or dashboards, Superset may ingest it as trusted input. This is interaction-based and not blocked by default.
conditions: IF Claude Code writes content into a shared repo or workspace that Superset later reads
IF Superset ingests file or API content without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict shared directories to read-only for one agent
Add a provenance header or filename convention for machine-generated files
Require manual review before Superset imports any Claude-produced artifact
Separate workspaces per agent
requires-engineering: add content-signing or provenance tracking

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, and runs as the invoking user with no self-isolation. Superset has allowlisted network egress and API access, so if sensitive files are placed in a shared workspace, Claude Code can read them and Superset may later expose derived data through its analytics surfaces. The pair creates a plausible shared-data leakage path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared cwd or repo
IF Superset is configured to query or display data derived from those files
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Mount sensitive inputs read-only and outside the repo
Use separate service accounts for each agent
Review Superset datasets before publishing
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, and modify_git_state; its concurrency model says shared state with other instances is via filesystem and git only. Superset is not runnable and only advertises allowlisted egress, so the main conflict is with Claude Code instances and any Superset-side artifacts in the same workspace. Because the pair can race on shared files/git without locking, default coordination is unsafe.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF git state or shared files are modified concurrently without locks
mitigations: Serialize writes with a lock file
Assign separate branches per agent
Disable concurrent runs on the same workspace
Review and merge changes manually
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, patches, and shell actions, while Superset can consume API-backed analytics inputs. If Superset treats Claude-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade from generated facts into dashboards or downstream decisions. The profiles do not show built-in verification between them, so the pathway exists in default use but is not guaranteed to be catastrophic.
conditions: IF Superset imports Claude-generated files, SQL, or metrics without validation
IF downstream users act on Superset outputs as authoritative
mitigations: Require human review of Claude outputs before import
Add schema validation on all imported artifacts
Compare dashboard results against a second source
Tag generated content as untrusted until verified
requires-engineering: implement automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, retention, or regulated-data handling mismatch is documented for Claude Code or Superset in the profiles. Claude Code does handle git credentials and local files, while Superset only shows allowlisted egress and API access. Because the evidence is sparse and no specific compliance breach is established, this is a low-confidence, low-severity documentation gap rather than a proven violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF Superset is configured to export or retain that regulated data outside policy
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling policies before use
Avoid placing regulated data in the shared repo
Review Superset retention settings
Limit Claude Code access to non-regulated projects
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
